title: Radish Sprout and Perilla Salad
shortDescription: Commercial radish sprouts and shredded perilla leaves are dressed immediately before service with rice vinegar, soy, gochugaru, and sesame.
culturalContext: This is a contemporary Korean-inspired fresh salad. Raw sprouts carry a distinct microbial risk that washing cannot eliminate; the descriptive Korean name and whether this dish is appropriate for publication require human review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

instructions.heading: Assess whether raw sprouts are appropriate
instructions.action: Do not serve this raw-sprout salad to pregnant people, young children, older adults, or people with weakened immune systems; choose a fully cooked alternative.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The intended diners are not in a higher-risk group.
instructions.safetyNote: Washing does not eliminate pathogens that may be inside sprout seeds.

instructions.heading: Check package and sprouts
instructions.action: Use a cold sealed in-date commercial package; discard slimy, moldy, discolored, warm, recalled, or off-smelling sprouts.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sprouts are crisp, cold, and fresh-smelling.
instructions.safetyNote: Check current recalls and never use home-grown sprouts in this draft.

instructions.heading: Rinse and dry
instructions.action: Rinse sprouts, perilla, and scallion under cool running water and dry thoroughly.
instructions.safetyNote: Rinsing reduces surface soil but does not make contaminated raw sprouts safe.

instructions.heading: Mix dressing
instructions.action: Whisk vinegar, soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, sesame oil, and seeds in a clean bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Verify soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame labels.

instructions.heading: Toss at service
instructions.action: Shred perilla on a clean board, add all greens, and toss immediately before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Greens are lightly coated and crisp.

instructions.heading: Serve immediately
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean dish and serve at once; discard table-exposed leftovers.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not store dressed raw-sprout leftovers for later service.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this is a raw ready-to-eat salad.
visualDonenessCues: No slime, mold, or off odor
foodSafetyNotes: Raw sprouts can harbor pathogens inside seeds; washing cannot eliminate this risk.
Higher-risk people should avoid raw sprouts and receive a fully cooked alternative.
Use only sealed refrigerated commercial sprouts, check recalls, and never use home-grown sprouts in this draft.
Keep at or below 40°F / 4°C, serve immediately, and discard leftovers.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels.

substitutions: For higher-risk diners, replace raw sprouts with a separately validated fully cooked vegetable.
ingredientSourcing: Buy sealed cold commercial radish sprouts within date and check current recall notices.
makeAhead: Mix dressing up to 1 day ahead; prepare sprouts only immediately before service.
storage: Keep unopened sprouts at or below 40°F / 4°C; serve the dressed salad immediately and discard leftovers.
reheating: Do not reheat; use a separately validated cooked alternative instead.
leftovers: Discard all dressed or table-exposed leftovers.
servingSuggestions: Serve only to diners for whom raw sprouts are appropriate.

faq.question: Does washing make raw sprouts safe?
faq.answer: No. Contamination can occur inside the seed where rinsing cannot reach.

faq.question: Who should avoid raw sprouts?
faq.answer: Pregnant people, young children, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems should choose a fully cooked alternative.
